{{Quote|Wanna drink?''"<br />"''I'm looking for someone.''"<br />"''Came to the right place.''"<br />"''A lowlife death stick dealer. Just came in here.''"<br />"''A lot of people come through here, friend.''|Bufon Taire and Jango Fett|<ref name="BH">''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]''</ref>}}
'''Bufon Taire''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who was the [[Bartender/Legends|chief bartender]] for the [[Outlander Club/Legends|Outlander Club]], located in the [[Uscru Entertainment District/Legends|Uscru Entertainment District]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Taire had a well-stocked bar with [[Color/Legends|color]]-coded ingredients, such as his famous "[[starshine special]]" additive. While working at the club in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Taire was approached by [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], who was seeking out the [[Death stick/Legends|death stick]] dealer [[Jervis Gloom]]. The bartender, threatened by Fett, revealed that Gloom took a lift to the club's [[Casino/Legends|casino]].

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Taire was again working at the club when Fett and his fellow bounty hunter [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]] met there to plan an [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|assassination attempt]] on [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]. Not long afterwards, Taire served a drink to [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] in the club while he and his [[Padawan/Legends|padawan]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] searched the club for Wesell, who had failed her assassnation. Taire noticed the bounty hunter approaching Kenobi from behind with a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]], just moments before Kenobi used his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] to [[Dismemberment/Legends|dismember]] her [[Limb/Legends|arm]].

==Biography==
===Bartending for clubgoers=== 
[[File:Outlander_Club.png|thumb|350px|right|Bufon Taire worked at the Outlander Club (pictured).]]
Bufon Taire was a [[Human/Legends|Human]]<ref name="FF20" /> [[Gender/Legends|male]]<ref name="CSWE" /> with connections to the criminal [[Baath brothers/Legends|Baath brothers]]. When the Baath brothers took over the [[Outlander Club/Legends|Outlander Club]],<ref name="Starships">{{StarshipsVehiclesCite|57|In A Galaxy Far, Far Away}}</ref> a [[Nightclub/Legends|nightclub]] and [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] hall located in the [[Uscru Entertainment District/Legends|Uscru Entertainment District]] of the<ref name="CSWE2">{{CSWECite|II|431|Outlander Club}}</ref> [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Complete">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]],<ref name="CSWE2" /> Taire was brought over to work as the [[Bartender/Legends|chief bartender]],<ref name="Starships" /> a top employee position.<ref name="FF96">{{FactFile|96|OUT 1-2|Outlander Nightclub Patrons}}</ref> 

His well-stocked bar at the center of the club featured the best<ref name="FF44">{{FactFile|44|COR 21-22|Coruscant &ndash; Outlander Club}}</ref> ingredients like [[Aludium pu-36]],<ref name="db" /> [[polyquaternium-7]], [[Insecticide/Legends|insecticide]],<ref name="TVD">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> and his famous and popular "[[starshine special]]" additive.<ref name="db" /> If Taire knew an individual, or if that individual was with the right people, they might have been treated to the "starshine special."<ref name="FF44" /> The ingredients were color-coded to better indicate toxicity among different [[Species/Legends|species]] and prevent customer [[Death/Legends|death]].<ref name="Starships" /> As an extra measure, Taire [[Water/Legends|watered]] down his drinks<ref name="db" /> with cheap, tasteless liquids<ref name="Starships" /> to be precautious<ref name="db">{{DB|location|outlandersclub|Outlander Club}}</ref> and maximize profits.<ref name="Starships" />

Taire worked alongside his assistant bartender [[Ganwick Trag]], and together they kept the drinks going in the club as most of the Outlander's action and gossip was spread around them.<ref name="FF96" /> Aside from Trag, Taire had another [[Bufon Taire's assistant bartender/Legends|assistant bartender]] who had been fired from some of the most respectful bars on Coruscant.<ref name="Complete" />

===Answering to a bounty hunter===
{{Quote|Listen, "friend." I'm giving you a chance to save your club.''"<br/>"''Please, don't shoot, I'm just a bartender! I don't want any trouble. I'm just trying to run a clean place, you know?''"<br/>"''I bet. Now where is he?''"<br/>"''He took a lift up to the casino.''"<br/>"''Call it down.|Jango Fett threatens Bufon Taire over the whereabouts of Jervis Gloom.|<ref name="BH" />}}
[[File:FettTaire-SWBH.png|thumb|left|350px|Jango Fett threatens Bufon Taire at the Outlander Club]]
After the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="BHDate">''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]'' is set immediately after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], which ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].</ref> Taire was working behind the bar of the club when the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] entered, seeking death stick dealer and clubgoer [[Jervis Gloom]].<ref name="BH" /> Fett approached Taire at the bar and said he was looking for someone. After the bartender deflected the statement, Fett pulled out one of his [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistols]] and threatened the bartender. Not wanting to get shot, Taire told Fett that Gloom took a lift up to the club's casino. The bounty hunter then ordered for Taire to call the lift down, to which the bartender obliged. When the lift came down, several thugs poured out, though Fett killed them all and went up to the casino to collect the bounty on Gloom.<ref name="BH" />

===Serving a Jedi===
{{Quote|Jedi business, go back to your drinks.|Anakin Skywalker, to Bufon Taire and other people in the Outlander Club|audio=Anakin-JediBusiness-AOTC.flac|<ref name="aotc">{{Film|II}}</ref>}}
In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="JFBHDate">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of {{Film|II}} to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. The scene from ''[[Jango Fett: Bounty Hunter]]'' in which [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] is in the [[Outlander Club/Legends|Outlander Club]] takes place immediately before the film, meaning it must be set in that [[Standard year/Legends|year]].</ref> Taire was bartending at the Outlander when the Jango Fett and the bounty hunter [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]] meet up there to plot an [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|assassination]] on the [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]].<ref name="Jango Fett: Bounty Hunter">''[[Jango Fett: Bounty Hunter]]''</ref> During a [[Standard day/Legends|night]]<ref name="aotc">{{Film|II}}</ref> not long after,<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of {{Film|II}} to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].</ref> Taire was again working behind the bar of the club when the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] entered, searching for Wesell her attempt on the senator's life failed. Kenobi eventually went up to the bar<ref name="aotc" /> and signaled him. The bartender served him a small glass with a luminescent [[Color/Legends|blue]] liquid, which Kenobi thanked him for. Taire proceeded to serve<ref name="aotc" /> the bounty hunter [[Kalyn Farnmir/Legends|Kalyn Farnmir]]<ref name="Kalyn Farnmir">{{DB|character|kalynfarnmir|Farnmir, Kalyn}}</ref> before leaving that side of the bar.<ref name="aotc" /> 

After the [[Slythmonger/Legends|slythmonger]] [[Elan Sel'Sabagno/Legends|Elan Sel'Sabagno]] left the bar, Kenobi tossed back the drink, which Taire refilled.<ref name="Novelization">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref> A short while later,<ref name="aotc" /> Taire noticed Wesell approaching Kenobi from behind with a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]],<ref name="SetPiece">{{InsiderCite|65|Set Piece|Set Piece: The Outlander Club}}</ref> just before the Jedi turned around and [[Dismemberment/Legends|dismembered]] her [[Limb/Legends|arm]] using his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]. Skywalker told the clubgoers to go back to their drinks and the Jedi left with the bounty hunter.<ref name="aotc" /> While the pair interrogated Wesell outside, Taire was no longer at the club's bar, but though his assistant bartender was.<ref name="Complete" />

==Personality and traits==
The no-nonsense<ref name="FF44" /> and ever-watchful<ref name="SetPiece" /> Taire had badly scarred<ref name="Starships" /> dark skin and brown [[Hair/Legends|hair]]. He had differently colored [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], with his right being white, and his left being brown.<ref name="CSWE" /> When Jango Fett threatened him, Taire claimed he just wanted to run a clean establishment and<ref name="BH" /> eagerly<ref name="HunterGuide" /> gave into his demands to call the Outlander Club's lift down.<ref name="BH" />

==Equipment==
While working at the Outlander Club,<ref name="Jango Fett: Bounty Hunter" /><ref name="JFBHDate" /><ref name="NEC" /> the bartender wore a dark blue [[Suit/Legends|suit]] with light gray sleeves and dark blue pants. The suit had a dark [[Metal/Legends|metal]] collar with glowing lapels.<ref name="FF96" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Skull-cracking bartender===
{{Quote|Close examination reveals that he sports facial scarring and mismatched eyes, implying that Taire would be able to crack a few skulls should a fistfight ever break out on the dancefloor|Daniel Wallace|<ref name="Who's Who" />}}
Bufon Taire was portrayed by an uncredited extra in the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']].<ref name="aotc" /> The Outlander Club scenes featuring the character were shot at [[Fox Studios, Sydney]] on [[July 17]], [[2000]].<ref name="Mythmaking">''[[Mythmaking: Behind the Scenes of Attack of the Clones]]''</ref> Prior to the film's release, Taire was first pictured in the documentary "[[Making Episode II Webdocs|A Twinkle Beyond Pluto]],"<ref name="ATBP">{{SW|url=video/a-twinkle-beyond-pluto|series=Making Episode II Webdocs|text=Part 5: A Twinkle Beyond Pluto}}</ref> released on [[July 31]], [[2001]].<ref name="ATBP Date">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/bts/me2/archive.html|text=''Making Episode II Webdocs'' archive}}</ref> The character then appeared in an illustration in the film's [[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones Movie Storybook|storybook]], written by [[Jane Mason]] and illustrated by [[Sarah Hines Stephens]]; its [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|novelization]] authored by [[R. A. Salvatore]];<ref name="Novelization" /> and in an illustration in the young readers book ''[[Jango Fett: Bounty Hunter]]'', written by [[Eric Arnold]] and illustrated by [[Valerie Reckert]].<ref name="Jango Fett: Bounty Hunter" /> All simultaneously released on [[April 23]], 2002.<ref name="JFBHRelease">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/young/news20020225.html|text=Book Preview: Episode II Children's Books}}</ref><ref name="StorybookRelease">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/young/news20020225.html|text=Book Preview: Episode II Children's Books}}</ref><ref name="Cargo Bay">{{RandomHouseOld|url=author/results.pperl?authorid=26771|text=R.A. Salvatore}}</ref> Episode II later released on [[May 16]], [[2002]].<ref name="Year">''[[Star Wars Year by Year: A Visual Chronicle]]''</ref> 

Taire was first given a name<ref name="FF44" /> around [[October 30]], 2002,<ref name="Date">{{FFdates|44}}</ref> with the publication of the [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 44|fourty-fourth]] issue of [[The Official Star Wars Fact File|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'']] magazine.<ref name="FF44" /> The name Bufon Taire is a homonym of "bouffant hair."<ref name="Who's Who" /> In the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]'',<ref name="Jango Fett: Bounty Hunter" /> released on [[November 22]], 2002,<ref name="Year">''[[Star Wars Year by Year: A Visual Chronicle]]''</ref> Taire was voiced by [[Kevin Michael Richardson]]. In the game<ref name="BH" /> and in its official guide written by [[David Hodgson|David Hodgsen]]<ref name="HunterGuide">[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: Bounty Hunter'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref> and released on [[November 26]], 2002,<ref name="Amazon">{{Amazon|url=Bounty-Hunter-Primas-Official-Strategy/dp/0761541640|text=Star Wars Bounty Hunter (Prima's Official Strategy Guide)}}</ref> Taire is identified simply as "bartender."<ref name="BH" /><ref name="HunterGuide" /> Additionally, Taire's model is reused for a bartender servicing a different bar in the Uscru District.<ref name="BH" /> 

In "[[Who's Who in the Outlander Club: It's Ladies' Night]]," an article published in the [[Star Wars Insider 75|seventy-fifth]] issue of ''[[Star Wars Insider]]''<ref name="Who's Who" /> on [[April 6]], [[2004]],<ref name="SW.com">{{SWArchive|url=community/fanclub/mag/news20040315.html|text=The New Face of Evil}}</ref> author [[Daniel Wallace]] stated that Taire's facial scarring implied that Taire could crack a few [[Skeleton/Legends|skulls]] should a fistfight ever break out on the dancefloor.<ref name="Who's Who" /> 

===Inconsistencies===
The novelization of Episode II incorrectly describes the drink he serves Obi-Wan Kenobi as amber-colored,<ref name="Novelization" /> despite it appearing luminescent blue in the movie.<ref name="aotc" /> The forty-fourth issue of the Fact File describes Taire as Human,<ref name="FF44" /> while the [[2008]] reference book ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' describes him as [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]].<ref name="CSWE" /> As sources published after ''The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia'' refer to the character as Human,<ref name="Starships" /><ref name="FF20" /> this article assumes the book is in error describing Taire as humanoid.
